canonical.queue_ids: request ids are replaced by apr-a0000000000N (N = 1-based enqueue order); apr-ffffffffffff is a literal unknown id; Go draws 6 random bytes
canonical.tokens: device bearer tokens are the placeholder {token:<device name>}; Go draws 20 random bytes per enrolment

scope.decision_order: listing order is newest first by creation instant; requests are enqueued in order with at least 5 ms between them
scope.expiry_cases: request expiry uses a 150 ms lifetime and a 450 ms settle pause; the recorded outcome (409 already expired / absent from the list) is not timing dependent beyond that margin
scope.mounting: the Go server mounts the handler on both patterns of an http.ServeMux when the approval handler option is given; the generator rebuilds that mux and pins the mounting source lines (mounting)
scope.not_recorded: HEAD requests, request bodies above the server limit and TLS/mTLS (transport layers owned by HTTP-001..004 fixtures)
scope.rate_limit: serverbootstrap wraps the chain in auth.RateLimiterMiddleware (default 60 requests/minute/IP); the Rust server has no rate limiter on any route, so no throttling case is recorded
scope.store_cleanup: Go also runs DeviceSessionStore.StartCleanup every 15 minutes; Validate rejects expired sessions regardless, so only the expiry itself is recorded
scope.transport: raw HTTP/1.1 over a loopback TCP listener serving the Go http.ServeMux; only Content-Type, X-Content-Type-Options and Location response headers are contract, Date/Content-Length/Connection are HTTP-library artefacts

cases.description: empty queue lists {"requests":[]}
pending requests newest first, Go HTML escaping, undecided decided_at is the zero time
r.URL.Path excludes the query
approved and expired requests leave the pending list
decided_by is the device id of the bearer, not its name; two devices
one trailing slash after the action is trimmed
no request body is read: malformed JSON (and any other body) does not change the decision
a decided request cannot be decided again; the conflict names the first decision
an expired request is not decidable
unknown id is 404 for approve and deny; nested ids are not special
the handler sees the decoded path
an authenticated POST to the bare subtree root has no id
an id without /approve or /deny suffix is an unknown action
401 for every Authorization value that is not exactly "Bearer <token>", list and decide
header names are case-insensitive
a token no device holds, including other bearer shapes (MCP legacy/scoped tokens are not device tokens)
a device revoked before the server loads its store is rejected; the other device still works
a session whose expires_at has passed is rejected
a revocation written by another store instance (the approval-revoke CLI) takes effect on the running server
an unauthenticated decide is 401 before the 400/404/409 route errors and never decides
only GET on the list path and POST below the subtree root are served; everything else is the mux 404 before authentication
ServeMux redirects an unclean path to its clean form before the handler runs
